I prefer defering this question to https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-subresource-integrity/issues/116.

As far as briefly skimmed, I feel both of full set or strongest metadata comarison would work (if the non-strongest part of the integrity metadata is virtually ignored and is no-op -- I'm not sure if I'm understanding correctly though), but not yet sure if strongest metadata comparison is sufficient.

Anyway the equality is used for the same purpose in multiple locations (here for module map, the other for link rel=preload), so https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-subresource-integrity/issues/116 is a better place to resolve this issue altogether.

In terms of implementation, Chromium uses full set equality for now (existing code for link rel=preload and https://crrev.com/c/8380928 for module map).

body:
We need to store the integrity metadata used for loading CSS/JSON/text modules (which has null fetch options currently), so just "dealing with null script fetch options" wouldn't work.

The candidate storage would be:

- module's script fetch options or in-progress module fetch record, depending on whether the module loadnig is done or still in progress (the current PR), or
- module map's value i.e. change the value type to the pair of (module script or list of algorithms, integrity), regardless of module loading state.

Either is fine with me (anyway the behavior is the same).
